'''Mark Samuel Nelkin''' (born 12 May 1931) is an American [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]].

Under the direction of Professor [[Hans Bethe]], he received his Ph.D. in theoretical physics from [[Cornell University]] in 1955. From 1955 to 1962 he worked in the nuclear industry for [[General Electric]] in [[Schenectady]] and [[General Atomic]] in San Diego. In 1962 he became a member of the Cornell faculty.<ref name=CornellBio>[https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/people/mark-nelkin/ Biography at Cornell Engineering website]</ref> He was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1968.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/mark-nelkin/|title=Mark Nelkin|publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|accessdate= 15 December 2018}}</ref> He retired from Cornell University as professor emeritus in 1993. After retirement he moved to New York City and remained active in refereeing articles for ''[[Physical Review Letters]]'', ''Physical Review E'', ''The Physics of Fluids'', and the ''Journal of Fluid Mechanics''.<ref name=CornellBio/>

{{blockquote|He spent leaves from Cornell at the University of Paris, The Collège de France in Paris, The National Bureau of Standards in Gaithersburg, Maryland, Harvard University, and the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences at New York University. At the Collège de France in 1976, he gave a series of twelve lectures on turbulence at the invitation of [[Pierre Gilles de Gennes]].<ref name=CornellBio/>}}

Nelkin became a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1984,<ref name="aps">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=10 June 2018}}</ref> having been nominated by their Division of [[Fluid dynamics|Fluid Dynamics]],<ref name="aps"/> for contributions to the advancement of [[physics]] by strong [[Theoretical physics|theoretical]] contributions in four areas beginning with the physics of [[thermal neutrons]] and its applications to [[Thermal-neutron reactor|nuclear reactors]], [[Kinetic theory of gases|kinetic theory]] of fluctuations in fluids, turbulence, and [[1/f noise]].

Nelkin was married to the American [[sociology of science|sociologist of science]] [[Dorothy Nelkin]] until her death in 2003.

==Publications==
* ''Does Kolmogorov mean field theory become exact for turbulence above some critical dimension?''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/2144437|title=Does Kolmogorov mean field theory become exact for turbulence above some critical dimension?|author=Mark Nelkin|date=1 April 2001|work=ResearchGate}}</ref>
